newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Lippo Group restructuring approved.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Lippo Group restructuring approved.

text.p: Widely diversified Indonesian conglomerate the Lippo Group won shareholder approval on Friday for a controversial restructuring of its three financial subsidiaries through internal acquisitions.

"We are happy the restructuring plan got strong support from shareholders. It shows that they believe this plan will reward all investors," Roy Tirtadji, managing director of the group told reporters after the plan was endorsed by shareholders of Lippo Life and Lippo Securities.

A Lippo Life proposal to buy an additional 40 percent stake in Lippo Bank was approved by 93 percent of its shareholders, Tirtadji said. Shareholders had earlier said the vote was approved by 61 percent of those voting.
The purchase will take Lippo Life's stake in Lippo Bank to 45 percent.
Later, shareholders of Lippo Securities unanimously approved a proposal to raise its stake in Lippo Life to 32 percent from the existing four percent.
The 875 billion rupiah ($380 million) restructuring will be funded mostly by loans.
Lippo Securities shareholders also approved a proposal to execute a one-for-one stock split, which requires approval from the Ministry of Justice.
Brokers have said the restructuring allows the Riady family, which controls Lippo, to cash out a large part of its holding in the group and does not otherwise provide many advantages.

But group deputy chairman James Riady has said all proceeds received by the family will be ploughed back in a rights offer to be made by Lippo Securities within 12 months. He has said the restructuring will create great synergy among the firms.

"The management of Lippo Life, Lippo Securities and Lippo Bank are very excited about the prospects of creating effective financial supermarkets, which will provide one-stop shopping to our more than 1.8-million-strong retail customer base and numerous corporate clients," said senior Lippo official Markus Parmadi.
